analyzed_vuln.description: In `blosc_d`, the decompression loop reads per-stream compressed sizes with `cbytes = sw32_(src)` after only checking `srcsize >= 4`, but it does not ensure `src` still points inside the actual chunk buffer for this iteration. With malformed frame/chunk metadata, `src_offset`/`srcsize` can become inconsistent with the true `src` pointer provenance, so `sw32_` dereferences an invalid address and crashes (wild read). The root cause is missing pointer/bounds validation in `blosc_d` before reading stream headers from attacker-controlled chunk data.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer passes attacker-controlled bytes to `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer`, then `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk` -> `frame_decompress_chunk` -> `blosc2_decompress_ctx` -> `blosc_d`. A crafted frame/chunk must survive earlier format checks and produce inconsistent internal offsets/sizes (e.g., via lazy/block metadata and stream layout fields) such that `blosc_d` enters the stream loop and calls `sw32_(src)` with an out-of-bounds/wild `src` pointer. This triggers a READ SEGV at `sw32_`.
